channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: A narrativa de que Trump ameaça o Pix não resiste à realidade
item.description: Lula, the PT, and their allies have revived the claim that the Pix payment system is under threat from the United States, linking it to the designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist groups and potential new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods. However, this narrative lacks factual basis, as there is no evidence the U.S. government intends or has the capacity to interfere with Brazil’s instant payment system.

item.title: Tribunal militar não pode rever provas de crime julgado no STF
item.description: The Military Court cannot review evidence of crimes already judged by the Supreme Federal Court, according to opinions from Judiciary and Public Ministry authorities. The column sought their views on whether the STM could revisit evidence of the coup plot to preserve the ranks of some defendants. The authorities' names were withheld.

item.title: ‘Bondades’ de Lula chegam a R$ 215 bi no ano eleitoral: 96% ficam fora do arcabouço fiscal
item.description: In the 2026 election year, the Lula government has launched economic measures totaling R$215 billion (1.6% of GDP), nearly double the additional revenues collected (R$109 billion, 0.8% of GDP). Of this amount, 96% fall outside the fiscal framework, raising concerns about public finance sustainability. The article notes these 'benevolences' aim to stimulate the economy but create substantial fiscal pressure.

item.title: Bolsonaristas da Bahia resistem a entrar em campanha por ACM Neto caso ex-prefeito não peça voto em Flávio
item.description: Members of Bahia's PL resist supporting ACM Neto in the gubernatorial race unless he backs Flávio Bolsonaro in the presidential race. A preliminary agreement exists for ACM Neto to support Ronaldo Caiado in the first round, with potential alignment with Flávio Bolsonaro in a possible second-round runoff against Lula. Bahia's right-wing asserts its support is not automatic and requires mutual dialogue, while the PT's Jerônimo Rodrigues seeks re-election in a technical tie according to recent polls.

item.title: Telão na rua, roda de samba e chope a cada gol: bares para assistir aos jogos do Brasil na Copa
item.description: The World Cup begins on June 11 and Brazil debuts on Saturday the 13th against Morocco. Several bars and restaurants in Rio de Janeiro are offering big screens, live music, beer promotions and snacks to watch the matches, including Antiquário do Breganha (Botafogo), Baródromo (Maracanã) and Beco do Rato (Lapa), featuring samba groups, live music sessions and tributes to carnival personalities like Mestre Ciça.

item.title: Equipe, memes e resposta a Flávio: entenda a queda de braço pela estratégia digital na pré-campanha de Lula
item.description: Lula’s 2026 re-election digital strategy is split between Communications Minister Sidônio Palmeira, who promotes national sovereignty and lighter content via Secom, and Nicole Briones and Ricardo Stuckert, who advocate for a more aggressive stance against rivals like Flávio Bolsonaro, particularly highlighting his ties to Daniel Vorcaro. Despite Sidônio’s close access to Lula, he does not control the president’s Instagram account — which has 14.7 million followers and is managed by Briones and Stuckert, who also oversee PT’s social media. The internal conflict centers on whether the campaign should adopt an institutional, conciliatory tone or a confrontational, polarizing one.

item.title: Orçamento paralelo: TCU investiga uso de 'dinheiro esquecido' de trabalhadores nos bancos para o Desenrola 2.0
item.description: The TCU is investigating the transfer of R$ 5.7 billion in 'forgotten money' from workers' bank accounts to the Fundo de Garantia de Operações (FGO), used to guarantee Desenrola 2.0, bypassing the federal budget and spending caps. The Desenrola 2.0 provisional measure revoked a legal provision requiring such funds to be directed to the National Treasury as primary budgetary revenue. While the government defends the program as essential for debt renegotiation, auditors challenge its accounting and budgetary treatment during an election year.

item.title: A agenda-bomba do Senado em ano eleitoral - O Assunto #1738
item.description: The Senate approved spending measures that will increase public expenditures by over R$ 2 trillion in ten years, including rural credit lines, salary raises for doctors and dentists, and relaxed retirement rules for health workers. The federal government warns it may challenge the measures in court, with STF Justice Gilmar Mendes suggesting they could be unconstitutional, while the Executive pushes for votes on its own priorities, such as public security and ending the 6x1 work scale. The approvals reflect growing tension between Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and President Lula in an election year.

item.title: Os signos dos jogadores da seleção podem ajudar o Brasil a conquistar o Hexa?
item.description: Astrology suggests that Brazil's national team, founded in 1914 under the sign of Cancer, possesses emotional unity and the ability to turn pressure into motivation. Players like Neymar (Aquarius), Vinícius Júnior and Endrick (both Cancer) bring creativity, loyalty, and boldness, while coach Carlo Ancelotti (Gemini) offers strategic flexibility. Planetary transits in 2026 indicate renewal and maturity, pointing to a favorable outlook in the pursuit of a sixth World Cup title.

item.title: Lula anuncia hoje cerca de R$ 4 bilhões em linha de crédito para entregadores
item.description: President Lula announces a subsidized credit line of approximately R$ 4 billion for motorcycle delivery workers, aimed at facilitating the purchase or replacement of motorcycles, including electric models. The financing will be backed by the FGO, with terms up to 48 months and payroll deductions via platform agreements (e.g., iFood), requiring at least six months of activity. The program targets 700,000 to 1.2 million workers who rely on motorcycles for income.

item.title: Copa do Mundo e São João devem reduzir votações no Congresso; veja propostas que podem ser afetadas
item.description: The World Cup and São João festivities are expected to slow legislative activity in Congress during June and July, with virtual sessions and facultative leave during Brazil’s matches. Controversial proposals such as ending the 6x1 work scale, the Security PEC, and reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16 are likely postponed to the second half of the year, compounded by the parliamentary recess (July 18–31) and party conventions in August. The stalled agenda and avoidance of contentious topics in virtual sessions contribute to a sluggish pace in the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Linha de crédito para entregadores deve ter carência de dois anos para início de pagamento
item.description: The federal government will launch a credit line for app-based delivery workers, featuring a two-year grace period before repayment begins, an annual interest rate of 12.5%, and a maximum loan of R$20,000 per worker to finance motorcycles up to 200cc or electric models. Eligibility requires at least six months of service with platforms like iFood, and the program will use FGO funds to cover potential defaults, targeting an estimated 700,000 to 1.2 million workers.

item.title: O Planalto contra-ataca: Motta e STF viram armas do governo para barrar ‘pauta-bomba’ do Senado
item.description: The federal government is leveraging President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s close relationship with House Speaker Hugo Motta and favorable ties with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to block the advancement of a rural debt renegotiation bill passed by the Senate, which the economic team estimates will cost R$ 140 billion over 13 years. The move aims to contain what the Planalto views as a 'budget bomb' threatening fiscal stability.

item.title: Fachin propõe reforma do Judiciário após desgaste de imagem do STF e quer fechar projeto até o final do ano
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin has established a panel of experts to draft a judicial reform addressing procedural delays, institutional transparency, artificial intelligence impacts, and declining public trust. The move follows months of controversies involving benefit payments, governance issues, the Banco Master scandal, and internal disputes that eroded the Court's image. While targeting completion by end-2026, the initiative prioritizes building internal consensus over rigid deadlines, aligning with parallel efforts like a judicial code of conduct and proposals by Minister Flávio Dino.

item.title: Livro propõe 'radicalização democrática' contra autoritarismo
item.description: A book proposes 'democratic radicalization' as a response to authoritarian risks in Brazil, citing Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 consultation with military leadership about overturning the election that Lula won. The proposal aims to strengthen democratic institutions against threats to the rule of law. The context reflects growing concern over democratic stability after the 2022 election.

item.title: Lula amplia coordenação de pré-campanha e instala comitê em Brasília
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has established part of his electoral committee in the Lago Sul neighborhood of Brasília and expanded the coordination of his pre-campaign for re-election in 2026. The move aims to strengthen the support structure for his continuity in power.

item.title: Governo tenta acordo com Alcolumbre para evitar desgaste na segurança e entre evangélicos
item.description: The Lula government is seeking an agreement with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) to prevent the voting of proposals that could cause electoral wear on security issues and among evangelicals. The move aims to protect Lula’s image ahead of the 2026 elections by containing sensitive agendas that could benefit the opposition.

item.title: 2º dia do Metrópoles Fashion & Design reúne moda, música e Copa do Mundo em Brasília
item.description: The second day of Metrópoles Fashion & Design brought together fashion, music, art, and live broadcasts of the 2026 World Cup matches at the National Museum of the Republic in Brasília. Now in its fourth edition, the event featured panels on creative economy, intellectual property in fashion, cultural appropriation, and AI’s impact, with experts like Beliza Euzébio and Ângelo Prata. Organized by Ilca Maria Estevão with support from the DF Tourism Secretariat, MFD continues to strengthen its role as a platform for local entrepreneurship and Brasília’s cultural scene.

item.title: Em Florianópolis, presidente do TSE defende o fortalecimento da coordenação da Justiça Eleitoral nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The president of the TSE, Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, advocated at the opening of the 91st Coptrel in Florianópolis for strengthening the institutional coordination of the Electoral Justice as an essential strategy for the success of the 2026 General Elections. He emphasized that challenges such as disinformation, AI, cybersecurity, and inclusion require integrated action among regional electoral courts.

item.title: Renan Santos ganha terreno em termômetro importante da eleição de 2026
item.description: In the social media landscape for the 2026 elections, Lula leads in audience with over 15 million followers, Flávio Bolsonaro maintains strong mobilization among supporters despite recent follower losses due to internal conflicts, and Renan Santos shows accelerated follower growth, indicating his ability to expand digital presence in a competitive environment.

item.title: Camilo contraria governo Lula e defende classificar facções como terrorismo
item.description: Former Education Minister Camilo Santana (PT-CE) opposed the federal government’s stance by advocating for the classification of criminal factions Comando Vermelho (CV) and Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) as terrorist organizations, arguing that the harshest possible measures should be applied. He criticized President Lula’s rejection of the U.S. designation as a threat to national sovereignty, stating he had advised Lula against opposing the classification and emphasized that security should not be politicized. Camilo also suggested the U.S. government could cooperate in combating organized crime.

item.title: Lula assina decretos e entrega títulos para oito territórios quilombolas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed 18 land titles for eight quilombola territories, benefiting 1,780 families across 11,673 hectares. This brings the total number of titles issued during his term to 74, covering 93,000 hectares — about 34% of all quilombola land titles ever granted by Brazil's Incra.

item.title: Haddad contesta sigilo de Tarcísio em contrato do metrô: "Ilegal"
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, denounced as illegal the secrecy imposed by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) over documents that would justify an additional R$ 3.7 billion expenditure on the concession of Metro Line 6 – Orange. Haddad argued that public contracts involving public funds cannot be kept secret, especially when the amount is so high and the public has a right to transparency. The state administration claims a 'geotechnical supervenience' as the cause of the delay, but the documentation proving this remains secret.

item.title: Em Belém, Flávio Bolsonaro diz que quer flexibilizar licenças ambientais para agronegócio e exploração mineral
item.description: In Belém, Flávio Bolsonaro advocated for relaxing environmental licensing to boost agribusiness and mining, claiming he will 'modernize legislation' to accelerate natural resource use in the Amazon. He also proposed hardening security policies, including classifying criminal factions as terrorists, lowering the age of criminal responsibility, and chemical castration for rapists. The senator is in pre-campaign for president and supports local candidacies in Pará.

item.title: Eduardo defende deputada Júlia Zanatta como vice na chapa de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro endorsed federal deputy Júlia Zanatta as the vice-presidential candidate on his brother Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket for the 2026 elections. The statement was made in a post on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter). The proposal aims to strengthen the alliance between São Paulo, Santa Catarina, and Rio de Janeiro within the PL party.

item.title: Moraes autoriza ex-servidor da Abin a ir à festa junina da filha
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes authorized former Abin employee Eduardo Arthur Izycki to attend his daughter's June festival in Brasília, despite being under precautionary measures in the Abin Paralela investigation. Izycki was indicted by the PF for fraud in bidding and qualified violation of functional secrecy, accused of leaking First Mile monitoring system data to counter a disciplinary proceeding at Abin.

item.title: Haddad diz que Lula refez “quase todos os contratos” de Tarcísio
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, accused the government of Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) of signing 'almost all' railway concession contracts poorly, forcing the Lula government to renegotiate them. He also criticized the partial privatization of Sabesp, completed in July 2024, calling the contract poorly drafted, predicting the company's profits will triple in two years while electricity bills rise, and stating consumers bear the cost. The São Paulo government did not respond to requests for comment.

item.title: Como Trump e Bolsonaro, Alcolumbre mira em Lula, mas acerta o Brasil
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre is using his institutional power to push legislative measures that strain public finances and challenge President Lula, framing them as political retaliation amid the 2026 election race. While the policies — rural debt relief, wage hikes for doctors, and benefits for health agents — have social merit, their timing and fiscal cost suggest a strategy aimed at weakening Lula rather than governing responsibly. The piece likens Alcolumbre’s conduct to that of Trump and the Bolsonaros, arguing that by confusing personal vendettas with national interest, he harms Brazil even when targeting Lula.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula vai a encontro de mulheres quilombolas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the 3rd National Meeting of Quilombola Women of Conaq in the Federal District, where he will sign decrees titulating new quilombola territories with an estimated expropriation value exceeding R$ 232 million and deliver titles to beneficiaries. Also present are Ministers of Racial Equality Raquel Barros and Agrarian Development and Family Agriculture Fernanda Machiaveli, along with First Lady Janja Lula da Silva.

item.title: PEC do Trabalho Flexível tem apoio de 38 senadores e rejeição de 26
item.description: The Flexible Work PEC, proposed by Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), has support from 38 senators and opposition from 26, falling short of the 49 votes needed for approval. Despite attempts by Cleitinho, Romário, and Zequinha Marinho to withdraw their signatures, the Senate rejected the requests, though the three later stated they support reducing the 6x1 work schedule. The PEC allows hiring based on actual hours worked, with proportional benefits and individual contracts overriding collective agreements on work hours.

item.title: Ronaldo Caiado é o primeiro presidenciável entrevistado na Sabatina da BP
item.description: Goiás Governor Ronaldo Caiado became the first presidential candidate interviewed in the BP Sabatina, launching the series of interviews with 2026 presidential contenders. The discussion covered key national policy topics, focusing on government proposals and stances on society’s main demands.

item.title: Augusto Nardes decide antecipar aposentadoria do TCU
item.description: Augusto Nardes, minister of the Tribunal of Accounts of the Union (TCU), announced the anticipation of his retirement for December 10, 2026, about 10 months before turning 75. The decision, formally communicated to his peers and the Chamber president, aims to allow the Chamber to plan the succession, as the vacancy belongs to the federal deputies' quota, opening space for political articulations, especially between PP and União Brasil. Nardes had considered running in the 2026 elections for PL in Rio Grande do Sul or the Federal District, but stepped back and will now support his daughter’s bid for a seat in the District Chamber of the DF.

item.title: Liberdade de expressão não pode ser seletiva; foi um erro censurar a pesquisa
item.description: Columnist Fernando Schüler criticizes the decision by TSE President Nunes Marques to suspend the release of an electoral poll showing declining voter intention for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro following the Banco Master revelations. He argues that censoring polls based on the potential influence of questions on respondents violates freedom of expression and improperly delegates censorship power to a court. Schüler maintains that the content of survey questionnaires is the sole responsibility of polling institutes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro quer uma vice mulher decorativa?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is seeking a female running mate to improve Bolsonarism's image among female voters, but faces internal resistance to more experienced candidates like Tereza Cristina. Names such as Julia Zanatta and Clarissa Tércio have been suggested, though seen as less effective as they primarily preach to the base. The campaign fears the pick may be perceived as merely decorative, reinforcing criticism that Bolsonarism lacks a genuine women's agenda.

item.title: Entra em vigor lei que estabelece política de recuperação da Caatinga
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has signed into law the National Policy for the Recovery of Caatinga Vegetation (Law 15.430/26), published in the Official Gazette. Originating from Bill PL 1990/24 by former Senator Janaína Farias, now mayor of Crateús (CE), the law mandates coordinated action among federal, state, municipal, and civil society actors to combat desertification, mitigate drought effects, prevent deforestation, and promote sustainable use of the Caatinga biome, including human resource training, technological development, and community participation.

item.title: Torcedores brasileiros fazem “bandeiraço” na Times Square
item.description: The partnership between Betnacional and the MVA promotes the 'Bandeiraço' in Times Square, New York, on the eve of Brazil's debut in the 2026 World Cup, expecting 3,000 to 5,000 Brazilian fans. The event features a samba school drumline, a monumental flag banner, Olinda-made dolls of Vini Jr. and Galvão Bueno, and digital activations on Times Square screens. Official gathering starts at 2 PM (NY time) at 5th & Mad bar, with the main event at 5 PM and closing at 7 PM, followed by digital display playback.

item.title: Sou da Paz responde Derrite sobre propostas para segurança pública
item.description: The Sou da Paz Institute responded to criticisms from pre-candidates Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP) and Delegado Felipe Curi (PP-RJ) regarding the 'Brazil in Action for Peace' proposal, advocating for the role of specialists and researchers in public safety policies and highlighting its 27 years of collaboration with police forces nationwide.

item.title: Governistas tentam acalmar os ânimos entre Lula e Alcolumbre
item.description: Government allies seek to ease tensions between Lula and Alcolumbre after the Senate rejected Jorge Messias for the STF, with Lula still upset and set to attend the G7 in France. The Senate is stalling the 6X1 end PEC while advancing controversial bills, including a R$140 billion agro credit line. Alcolumbre is likened to Eduardo Cunha for his confrontational legislative tactics.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Bolsonarismo “raiz” quer Flávio com discurso mais ideológico | HORA H
item.description: The more radical wing of Bolsonarism is urging pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro to adopt a more ideological discourse in the 2026 elections, prioritizing conservative right-wing agendas over moderation. This internal current aims to reinforce the candidate's ideological identity, aligning him more closely with the legacy of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The movement reflects tensions between pragmatic and radical factions within Bolsonarism.

item.title: ‘Pautas-bomba’ em tramitação no Congresso têm impacto fiscal de R$ 111 bilhões por ano, diz governo
item.description: The federal government disclosed that nine 'bombshell' proposals currently under consideration in Congress have an annual fiscal impact of R$ 111 billion, affecting public accounts through revenue foregone and mandatory spending. Key proposals include rural debt renegotiation (R$ 140 billion over 13 years), raising the Simples Nacional threshold (R$ 50 billion/year), and expanding the Municipal Participation Fund (R$ 10 billion/year). The Lula administration expressed concern over the fiscal imbalance caused by these measures, some already approved in the Senate and pending review in the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Nunes Marques articula consenso no julgamento da AtlasIntel
item.description: TSE President Justice Kássio Nunes Marques is seeking consensus to establish a rule banning the use of audio and video in electoral polls, following the AtlasIntel survey of May 19 that showed a drop in Flávio Bolsonaro’s popularity after exposing him in an audio with Daniel Vorcaro. Despite a request for vista by Justice Estela Aranha, Nunes Marques and Dias Toffoli argue the case should set a precedent on polling methodologies to avoid inducing voter responses. The goal is to send a message to pollsters, campaigns, and regional electoral courts about media influence on 'useful voting' perceptions, with expectations of a majority to approve the rule even without full unanimity.

item.title: Lula pressiona Márcio França em um xadrez que envolve palanques para a eleição
item.description: Lula is pressing Márcio França to abandon his Senate bid and become Fernando Haddad’s running mate in São Paulo to resolve a conflict over two Senate seats contested by Marina Silva and Simone Tebet. The maneuver is part of a broader negotiation involving PSB support for Lula’s allies in Minas Gerais and Pernambuco, and the PSB’s concession of its party label to host Tebet’s campaign after she left the MDB. França has previously yielded to Lula’s pressure, sacrificing candidacies for ministerial posts, but now faces a more intricate political chessgame spanning multiple states.

item.title: PT aciona STF e PF contra ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) filed representations with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) and the Federal Police (PF) requesting an investigation into the funding of 'Dark Horse', a biopic about former President Jair Bolsonaro. The PT alleges that some of the film's financing may have been illicitly sourced, potentially involving money laundering or illegal electoral contributions.

item.title: Lula promete zerar fila do INSS até setembro
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced that the new INSS president, Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, pledged to clear the backlog of benefit requests by September 2026, following a 15.4% drop from April to May, reducing pending claims from 2.6 million to 2.2 million. The decline began in March, one month before Gilberto Waller’s dismissal, and may be linked to INSS Normative Instruction PRES/INSS No. 203, which bars duplicate applications. Lula reaffirmed his 2022 campaign promise, stating that staffing or competency gaps must be addressed through hiring or replacements.

item.title: Lula confirma promessa de zerar fila de pedidos represados do INSS antes da eleição
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva confirmed that the government will clear the backlog of INSS benefit requests by September, ahead of the 2026 elections. The announcement was made during a ceremony at the Planalto Palace, emphasizing social security as a key electoral priority.

item.title: Presidente do INSS prometeu zerar fila até setembro, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reiterated, during a ceremony at the Palácio do Planalto, the promise to clear the INSS benefits waiting list by September, as assured by the institute’s new president, Ana Cristina Silveira. The backlog, which reached a record 3.1 million in February, has long been tied to a 2022 campaign pledge. Lula emphasized the April leadership change, replacing Gilberto Waller with career servant Ana Cristina, to expedite the resolution.

item.title: Sem acordo sobre urgência, Motta cede e define relator de projeto do governo sobre o fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Chamber President Hugo Motta appointed Leo Prates as rapporteur for the government's workweek reduction project after failing to remove constitutional urgency. The government retained urgency on its bill, while Motta pushed forward with the previously approved PEC to avoid legislative blockage before the July recess. The conflict highlights a power struggle between the Executive and Legislative branches, with the government linking its stance to rural debt renegotiation.

item.title: Ministros tentam reaproximar Lula de Alcolumbre após avanço de pauta-bomba no Senado
item.description: Ministers and political leaders are seeking to reconcile President Lula with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre following their rift after the Senate rejected Lula’s nominee, Jorge Messias, for the STF. Defense Minister José Múcio Monteiro, a mutual friend, is mediating the effort, though Lula has yet to schedule a meeting. The push comes amid heightened tension due to Senate approval of fiscally impactful measures, including debt renegotiation for large rural producers (minimum R$140 billion/year for a decade), wage increases for doctors and dentists, and special retirement for health agents.

item.title: Férias de julho: pesquisa aponta quais são os destinos mais desejados
item.description: Gramado (RS) leads Brazilian search trends for July 2026 vacations, with more than double the searches of the second-place destination, followed by Northeastern beach destinations occupying six of the top ten spots. Internationally, Bariloche tops searches, with Ushuaia and Santiago highlighting winter travel interest and Punta Cana and Cancún maintaining Caribbean appeal, while Buenos Aires reflects sustained interest in major cities.

item.title: Lula diz que INSS tem meta de zerar fila de espera para concessão de benefícios até setembro
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced that the INSS aims to eliminate the backlog of benefit applications by September 2024, fulfilling a 2022 campaign promise. New INSS president Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, appointed in April after Gilberto Waller’s dismissal, oversees a decline in pending requests from 3.1 million in February to 2.2 million currently, with average processing time dropping from 59 to 40 days. The target excludes documentation-related delays by beneficiaries, which account for over 20% of the backlog.
